checks.claim: C1: The descending all-vector-increment elimination invariant holds: exactly one surviving covariance at each closing label and none at each opening label, for arbitrary pairings, block roots and empty chains.
checks.reason: In increment coordinates each Green factor depends only on its own increment y_l. The position x_l is the sum of the increments with labels in [b(l), l] of its own block chain, so it involves only labels <= l. Invariant: before label l, the surviving covariances are exactly the pairs whose closing label is <= l. This holds at l=2k. At a closing label l with pair (i,l), x_l-x_i=y_l+z, where z involves only labels < l; this covers the same-chain, cross-chain and adjacent (z=0) cases. Every other surviving pair closes below l, so both of its endpoints are < l and it does not involve y_l. The bound sup_z depends only on h_l, and Tonelli (with y_{2k} innermost) removes the pair. At an opening label, the partner is larger and its pair is already removed; every surviving pair closes below l, so y_l enters only through G and integrates to h_l. The invariant then passes to l-1. Later positions do depend on y_l, but their covariances have already been replaced by h-only constants. The argument uses only label comparisons, so it is dimension-free and covers m=0, m=2k and every D, including domestic pairs. Each label is exactly one opening or one closing, which gives k of each. Hand checks: for (0,2) and (1,1) in d=1 white noise, the bound c*h_1/2 dominates the exact values.

checks.claim: C2: The direct d=1 Riesz and white convolution bounds, the uniform Gaussian averaging, and all constants are correct.
checks.reason: For even f that is nonincreasing in |y|, an interval of fixed length captures the most mass when centered at 0. So sup_z (1/2)c|y+z|^{-alpha} integrated over |y|<h equals c*h^{1-alpha}/(1-alpha) exactly. For gamma_eps=p_eps*gamma, Tonelli writes the smoothed integral as a mass-one p_eps(w)dw average of shifted integrals, so the same sup bounds it. White case: gamma_eps=c*p_eps and G<=1/2 give c/2. Both bounds are independent of eps and allow pair-dependent widths. This covers gamma_{2eps} in the source's (2.23) and gamma_{eps+eps~} in (2.11), as seen on the page images. No pointwise delta value is used, because S_{D,eps} is an ordinary integral.

checks.claim: C3: Weighted AM-GM, the k-power and the exact common spatial bound are correct, with no illegal negative weights.
checks.reason: The weights are 1 at the k openings and 1-alpha>0 at the k closings, total W=bk. Weighted AM-GM with x_l=h_l/w_l gives prod h^w <= (sum h/W)^W prod w^w <= (2t/(bk))^{bk}(1-alpha)^{(1-alpha)k}. Times (c/(1-alpha))^k this is [c 2^{2-alpha}(1-alpha)^{-alpha}(2-alpha)^{-(2-alpha)}]^k t^{bk}k^{-bk}, exactly K_sp; replacing c by V gives K_sp^gen. At alpha=1 the closing weight is 0, and the text correctly switches to ordinary AM-GM over the k openings only: (pi V/2)^k (2t/k)^k = (pi V)^k t^k/k^k, and likewise (c/2)^k(2t/k)^k = c^k t^k/k^k for d=1 white noise. No formula divides by 1-alpha at the endpoint. The constraint sum h <= 2t holds on [0,t]^m_< x [0,t]^{2k-m}_< after the chain reversal. The constants do not depend on k, m, D, any smoothing parameter or t.

checks.claim: C4: The common full temporal kernel is introduced before the sum symmetry; the ordered block factor, cube integral, pairing and split counts, and the regularized coefficient inequality are correct.
checks.reason: From chen-13 (2.24) and chen-09 (2.11), 0 <= gamma^0_delta(u) <= Gamma(alpha0)^{-1} int_0^inf e^{-lambda|u|} lambda^{alpha0-1} d lambda = |u|^{-alpha0}. Each regularized diagram is therefore bounded by its spatial factor times prod|s_i-s_j|^{-alpha0}. The spatial factor is bounded by a constant uniform in D and s, and only then is the sum over D taken (max_D S_D times sum_D T_D). F_k is invariant under all label permutations, because each permutation maps Pi_k bijectively. Block-preserving permutations tile [0,t]^{2k} into m!(2k-m)! copies of the ordered domain, and ties are null. The integral of |s-r|^{-alpha0} over [0,t]^2 is 2t^{2-alpha0}/((1-alpha0)(2-alpha0)) = Z t^{2-alpha0}. Disjoint pairs give P_k(Z t^{2-alpha0})^k, and P_k = (2k)!/(2^k k!). The split sum is 4^k/(2k)!. The product is (2ZK)^k t^{beta k}/(k! k^{bk}), with b+2-alpha0 = beta. Factors of 2 enter only through 4^k/2^k and through the 2t constraint inside K, so none is double-counted. Wick (2.23) has coefficient one per D, and A_k counts both (m,n) and (n,m).

checks.claim: C5: The low-alpha spectral estimate is correct: scaling of mu as a measure, finiteness of V, the exact layer-cake identity without isotropy or density assumptions, Fourier Fubini, and the sign/nonnegativity assumptions.
checks.reason: gamma(c.) has spectral measure equal to the pushforward of mu under xi -> c xi. Homogeneity and Fourier uniqueness on tempered distributions give mu(A/c) = c^{-alpha} mu(A), hence mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A). So mu(B_R) = V R^alpha, and V < infinity because mu is Radon. Continuity gives mu({0}) = 0 and null spheres. The layer cake gives int min{h,|xi|^{-1}} d mu = int_0^h mu(|xi| <= 1/u) du = V h^{1-alpha}/(1-alpha) for alpha<1; this uses only ball masses. e^{-eps|xi|^2/2} mu is finite by polynomial ball growth, so gamma_eps is the continuous Fourier transform of a finite measure, and it equals p_eps*gamma pointwise. G_{h,eta} has mass h (chen-07 (2.4)). Fubini is therefore absolute and gives multiplier e^{-eta|.|^2/2} sin(h|xi|)/|xi|, with |sin(hr)/r| <= min(h, 1/r). Nonnegativity: a nonnegative distribution is a positive measure, so gamma_eps >= 0, and G_{h,eta} >= 0. No positivity of the oscillatory integrand is asserted. The axis-supported example |x_1|^{-alpha} in d=2,3 is legitimately covered. Cross-check: the direct d=1 Riesz sup is exact, so the Fourier constant necessarily satisfies V >= c. This is consistent with calling the d=1 constants sharper.

checks.claim: C6: Degree-one endpoint: mu = dr sigma from annular rectangles, total sigma = V, evenness, the correct antipodal count, Gaussian 1D Fourier inversion I = pi(g_h*p), and the bound pi V/2. Also d=1 white V = c/pi, with no use of the divergent absolute envelope.
checks.reason: Sectors scale as R*sigma(E), so the polar rectangles (r1,r2] x E have mass (r2-r1)sigma(E). These form a pi-system generating the Borel sets of R^d minus {0}, and the measures are sigma-finite, so uniqueness gives mu = dr (x) sigma under the polar map. sigma(S^{d-1}) = mu(B_1 minus {0}) = V. A real stationary covariance is even, and Fourier uniqueness makes mu and sigma even. With a = (eps+eta)/2 > 0, the absolutely convergent double integral gives int sigma(d theta) int_0^inf e^{-ar^2} sin(hr)/r e^{ir theta.z} dr. Evenness of sigma turns the exponential into cos(r theta.z) with no factor 2. In 1D, g_h = (1/2)1_{|v|<h} has transform sin(hr)/r, and p_{2a} has transform e^{-ar^2}. Inversion with 1/(2 pi) and folding r to -r gives (g_h*p_{2a})(v) = (1/pi) I_a(h,v); the inversion is valid because the product is in L^1 and g*p is continuous. So 0 <= I_a <= pi/2, and the integral against sigma is at most pi V/2. In d=1 with gamma = c*delta_0: mu = c d xi/(2 pi), V = c/pi, and sigma({+1}) = sigma({-1}) = c/(2 pi). This gives c(g_h*p)(z) <= c/2, which matches the direct bound exactly, and K = pi V = c. Independent cross-check, d=3 with gamma = |x|^{-1}: mu = |xi|^{-2} d xi/(2 pi^2), so V = 2/pi and pi V/2 = 1. Newton's theorem gives int G_h(dy)|y+z|^{-1} = h*min(1/h, 1/|z|) <= 1, so the bound is attained. The absolute envelope is used only for alpha<1.

checks.claim: C7: Dimension-3 Green approximation: positivity and mass, weak product-measure limits at fixed noise, bounded continuous Wick covariances, joint-eta Cauchy in L2, the correct eta-first/noise-second limit order, and the mixed L1 transfer.
checks.reason: chen-13/14 define the d=3 integral by taking eta -> 0 first and then (eps,delta) -> 0. G_{h,eta} = p_eta*G_h is a nonnegative density of mass h with multiplier modulus <= 1, so both convolution lemmas hold uniformly in eta >= 0. At fixed (eps,delta), gamma^0_delta is bounded (gamma^0_delta(0) is finite) and gamma_{2eps} is bounded and continuous. The Wick sums for E[Y_eta Y_eta'] are therefore bounded continuous functions of linear combinations of increments. The increments are integrated against prod G_{h_l,eta} (x) prod G_{h_l,eta'}, which converges weakly with unchanged masses. The dominator C*prod h_l on bounded simplices gives dominated convergence in time. The joint limit does not depend on the rates, so the family is L2-Cauchy, and Cauchy-Schwarz passes the products to L1. The noise limit then uses chen-22 Theorem 4.1 (L2 limit for every n under (1.5)), and the products again converge in L1. Finitely many splits at fixed k and uniform bounds transfer the inequality to A_k(t). In d=1,2 only the noise limit is needed; the d=2 density is integrable, so Tonelli applies.

checks.claim: C8: The factorial direction, the scalar q-series bound, the k=0 term, the exact beta/q = kappa, and constants independent of degree, noise and time.
checks.reason: k! <= k^k gives k^{bk} >= (k!)^b, so k! k^{bk} >= (k!)^{b+1} = (k!)^q; this is the correct direction. For q >= 1 and nonnegative terms, sum a_k^q <= (sum a_k)^q, which gives sum z^k/(k!)^q <= exp(q z^{1/q}). With z = 2ZK t^beta, beta/q = (4-alpha-alpha0)/(3-alpha) = kappa, consistent with (E:kappa). A_0 = 1 is the k=0 term. The result C_2^gen = q(2ZK^gen)^{1/q} holds for every t>0. At alpha=1, q=2 and kappa = (3-alpha0)/2, which reproduces the writer's exp{2 sqrt(2Z pi V) t^{(3-alpha0)/2}}. The constants depend only on (alpha, alpha0, c or V).

checks.claim: C9: One-chain calibration, the p=1 lower bound and Jensen; the static exponent; the sharper d=1 normalized white check; no claim of variational-constant equality.
checks.reason: A single chain has sum h <= t, so the spatial bound applies with t/2, and the ordered-simplex integral of F_k is P_k(Z t^{2-alpha0})^k/(2k)!. The product is (ZK/2^{b+1})^k t^{beta k}/(k! k^{bk}) with b+1 = q. Hence C_1 = q(ZK)^{1/q}/2 and C_2/C_1 = 2^{1+1/q} = 2^{(4-alpha)/(3-alpha)}. Expectations of the L2 partial sums converge, and odd terms vanish. The imported lower bound of Theorem 1.2 requires (1.8)-(1.9) with 0<alpha<d or alpha=d=1 (chen-03), which every stated case meets. Under that hypothesis it forces L_* <= C_1. Then C_1 > 0 gives 2C_1 < C_2, consistent with Jensen. This is a logical consequence, as the text says, not a numerical evaluation of E_*. As alpha0 -> 0, kappa -> (4-alpha)/(3-alpha), stated as an exponent calibration only. With c_alpha = (1-alpha)/2, K_sp = 2^{1-alpha}(1-alpha)^{1-alpha}/(2-alpha)^{2-alpha} -> 1 as alpha -> 1. The white checks also hold: the ratio 2Z/(2c_0) = 2(3-alpha0) > 4, and the static order-4 bound (2Z)^2/(2*4) = 1/2 >= 11/540.

checks.claim: C12: Overall hidden assumptions or gaps, and substantive changes since v1.
checks.reason: I found no genuine gap. There are three substantive additions since the v1 d=1 review. (i) L:low-alpha-convolution: a measure-scaling and layer-cake Fourier bound valid for anisotropic or singular mu. (ii) L:alpha-one-convolution: a polar decomposition with exact 1D Gaussian inversion, avoiding the divergent absolute envelope. (iii) Transfer of the dimension-free elimination and temporal symmetry to d=2,3, with an explicit eta-first L2-Cauchy argument. The hidden assumptions are all standing ones: gamma real, even, nonnegative and nonnegative definite (so mu is positive and tempered); homogeneity understood distributionally; and the source's p_eps Gaussian convention, whose variance normalization does not affect any bound. The G0/G1 inputs are applied within their stated hypotheses.

minor: L:alpha-one-convolution sets a = (eps+eta)/2, which assumes covariance width eps. The source's mixed moments use gamma_{2eps} ((2.23)) or gamma_{eps+eps~} ((2.11)), which give a different a > 0. The bound is independent of a, so nothing breaks. A sentence saying that any covariance width eps' > 0 is allowed would align the text with the source.

The Brownian convention for p_eps (multiplier e^{-eps|xi|^2/2}) relies on the source's (1.20), which is not in the packet. Only positivity of a matters, so this is a pinpoint gap, not a mathematical one.

L:low-alpha-convolution goes from 'Gaussian weighting gives a finite measure' to Fourier Fubini without stating that gamma_eps equals, pointwise, the continuous Fourier transform of the finite measure e^{-eps|xi|^2/2}mu. That is the identity Fubini actually uses. One sentence would close it.
In the layer-cake step, the remark 'the endpoint of each indicator has no effect' implicitly uses mu(sphere) = 0, which follows from continuity of V R^alpha. This could be stated.

'Separate sharper Riesz constants in dimension one' is asserted without a displayed comparison. It holds because the direct d=1 Riesz convolution bound is the exact supremum, so necessarily V >= c_alpha; for example V/c is about 1.60 at alpha = 1/2. A one-line remark would justify the word 'sharper'.
The G0 route item still cites (4.4) for Theorem T:crude; R:source-uniformity identifies (5.4) as the relevant bound. This is legacy exposition outside Section 5.
